title: Genocide in Gaza
statement: Israel’s actions in Gaza since 7 October 2023 constitute genocide against Palestinians under the definition in the 1948 Genocide Convention.

fact_questions.prompt: Under Article II of the Genocide Convention, what intent distinguishes genocide from other atrocities?
options: The intent to destroy a protected group, in whole or in part, as such
The intent to defeat an enemy militarily despite expecting heavy civilian losses
The intent to displace residents from an area while preserving them as a group
The intent to punish a government through unlawful attacks on civilian property
fact_questions.explanation: Genocide requires prohibited acts and the specific intent to destroy a protected group as such. Knowledge that civilians will suffer, or intent to commit another grave crime, is not automatically the same mental element.
fact_questions.source_name: United Nations — Genocide Convention, Article II
fact_questions.importance_rationale: The specific-intent requirement is central to the proposition.
fact_questions.gateway_rationale: The specific-intent requirement is central to the proposition.

fact_questions.prompt: In its January 2024 Gaza order, how did the ICJ treat Palestinians when considering the Genocide Convention’s protected-group requirement?
options: As excluded from protection unless Palestinian statehood was first universally recognized
As a protected group, with Palestinians in Gaza forming a substantial part
As protected only if their religious identity could be separated from their national identity
As outside the Convention because Hamas also claimed to represent them politically
fact_questions.explanation: The ICJ considered Palestinians a protected group and Palestinians in Gaza a substantial part of that group. This addresses a necessary legal element; it does not itself establish prohibited acts or an intent to destroy the group.
fact_questions.source_name: International Court of Justice — Summary of order, 26 January 2024
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Replaces abstract group-list recall with whether the population in this proposition satisfies a necessary legal element.

fact_questions.prompt: Can deliberately imposing starvation or other destructive living conditions constitute genocide without directly shooting or bombing every victim?
options: No, because deaths through hunger or disease are excluded when they occur during an armed conflict rather than peacetime
Yes; any restriction contributing to hunger is sufficient
Yes, if both the destructive-conditions element and the required intent are established
No; most of the group must also be directly killed
fact_questions.explanation: Article II includes deliberately inflicting living conditions calculated to cause physical destruction. The prohibited act and specific intent must be established; deprivation is not excluded merely because death is indirect.
fact_questions.source_name: United Nations — Genocide Convention, destructive conditions of life
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Food, water and healthcare deprivation are central to the alleged conduct.
fact_questions.gateway_rationale: Food, water and healthcare deprivation are central to the alleged conduct.

fact_questions.prompt: What happened to stored reproductive material at Gaza’s Al-Basma fertility centre, according to the UN Commission of Inquiry’s March 2025 report?
options: The material was reported safely transferred abroad before the centre suffered damage
The centre lost administrative records, but its stored embryos and other material remained intact
The report found that all reproductive services had resumed normally across Gaza by January 2025
Shelling reportedly destroyed around 4,000 embryos and additional stored reproductive material
fact_questions.explanation: The Commission reported destruction of embryos and other reproductive material and no assisted reproductive services known to be available by January 2025. It linked wider healthcare destruction to alleged genocidal acts. Destruction and loss of reproductive capacity do not alone prove an intent to prevent births or destroy the group.
fact_questions.source_name: UN Commission of Inquiry — Sexual and reproductive violence report, 13 March 2025
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Replaces a legally listed act with no demonstrated application in the bank by concrete evidence relevant to reproductive survival in Gaza.

fact_questions.prompt: What minimum death toll does the Genocide Convention prescribe before conduct can count as genocide?
options: It prescribes no fixed numerical death threshold
At least half of the entire protected group must die
More than 100,000 members must be killed in one year
More deaths than in a previous recognized genocide
fact_questions.explanation: The Convention sets out acts and intent, not a fixed body count. Case law requires an intended targeted part to be substantial; numbers inform the assessment but do not replace the legal elements.
fact_questions.source_name: International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia — Krstić appeal, substantial-part requirement
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Prevents casualty rankings from becoming a substitute for the legal test.

fact_questions.prompt: According to ICJ case law, is forced removal of an ethnic population automatically genocide?
options: Yes; any organized expulsion of a protected ethnic community is legally sufficient proof of an intent to destroy that community
No; expulsion and physical or biological destruction are distinct
No; displacement cannot contribute to genocide in any context
Yes; expulsion counts as genocide if it crosses an international border, while otherwise identical internal displacement cannot
fact_questions.explanation: The Court distinguishes expulsion from destruction. Forced removal can still be a grave crime, and can form part of genocide if the acts and destructive intent are established.
fact_questions.source_name: International Court of Justice — Croatia v. Serbia, 2015 judgment
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Clarifies the distinction between ethnic cleansing and genocide without excusing either.

fact_questions.prompt: What distinguishes the legal category of crimes against humanity from genocide?
options: It requires an armed conflict and a larger death toll, whereas genocide can apply to any widespread civilian attack in peacetime
It requires victims from a single protected ethnic group
It can involve widespread or systematic attacks on civilians without the specific intent to destroy a protected group
It requires proof of a personal racial motive for every perpetrator
fact_questions.explanation: The categories have different elements and can overlap. Mass murder or persecution may qualify as crimes against humanity even if genocide’s specific intent is not proved. Moral condemnation does not depend on securing the genocide label.
fact_questions.source_name: International Committee of the Red Cross — International crimes
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Keeps classification separate from whether severe wrongdoing occurred.

fact_questions.prompt: When inferring genocidal intent solely from a pattern of conduct, what test did the ICJ apply in Croatia v. Serbia in 2015?
options: Intent must be a plausible inference, even if alternatives are equally reasonable
Intent must be expressed in a signed order and can never be inferred
Intent is presumed whenever civilian deaths exceed combatant deaths
Genocidal intent must be the only reasonable inference from the pattern
fact_questions.explanation: The Court allowed inference from conduct but required the inference of genocidal intent to be the only reasonable one. This is a merits standard for that mode of proof, not the test for interim protective measures.
fact_questions.source_name: International Court of Justice — Summary of judgment, 3 February 2015
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Defines the demanding inference test central to contested interpretations of the evidence.

fact_questions.prompt: At Auschwitz, what happened to some Jewish deportees whom the Nazis selected as fit for work?
options: They were temporarily kept alive for forced labour while other deportees were murdered
They received permanent protection from later selections and the wider policy of extermination
Their survival meant the authorities abandoned the killing of Jewish deportees as a group
They were generally released to return to their homes once assigned a civilian occupation
fact_questions.explanation: The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM) documents temporary selection for forced labour within the Holocaust. Survival, exemption or exploitation of some members can coexist with genocidal policy. That historical fact rebuts an automatic inference from survivors, but does not establish that a different war has the same intent.
fact_questions.source_name: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum — Selections upon arrival at Auschwitz
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Replaces familiar identification of the Holocaust with a fact that tests whether sparing some people necessarily disproves group-destructive intent.

fact_questions.prompt: How did the 1994 genocide against Tutsi civilians in Rwanda relate to the war against the Tutsi-led Rwandan Patriotic Front (RPF)?
options: The genocide began only after the rebels had surrendered and the military conflict was over
The genocide and the government’s military conflict with the rebels occurred together
The government’s war against the rebels made all Tutsi civilians lawful military targets
The genocide finding concerned only rebel soldiers killed while actively fighting government troops
fact_questions.explanation: The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM) describes a campaign against Tutsi civilians amid civil war, ending when the RPF seized Kigali. A real armed enemy and military conflict did not exclude genocide against civilians. The presence of Hamas therefore cannot alone settle the Gaza allegation; actual acts and intent still need examination.
fact_questions.source_name: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum — The Rwanda genocide
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Replaces victim-group name recall with an established case testing whether a genuine military conflict automatically excludes genocide.

fact_questions.prompt: Why did the international tribunal recognize Srebrenica as genocide although women and children were expelled and the mass executions mainly targeted men and boys?
options: The tribunal’s assumption that every military-age male was civilian
The rule that ethnic-conflict massacres require no proof of intent
The killings were part of an intended destruction of the Bosnian Muslim community of Srebrenica
The tribunal required proof that all Bosnian Muslims throughout the country had already been killed
fact_questions.explanation: The genocide finding concerned destruction of a substantial part of the protected group. The demographic pattern of victims did not exclude genocide; selecting men for execution did not establish that each was an active fighter.
fact_questions.source_name: International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia — Krstić appeal summary
fact_questions.importance_rationale: A legally established case tests claims that sparing some demographics necessarily disproves genocide.

fact_questions.prompt: Why did the ICJ reject Croatia’s genocide claim against Serbia in 2015 despite findings of killings and serious harm?
options: All the reported killings were found to have been invented
Genocide was proved but the Court lacked jurisdiction
The killings were all found lawful as wartime reprisals
The specific intent to destroy the Croat group was not proved
fact_questions.explanation: The Court found prohibited physical acts but not the specific destructive intent required for genocide. This is a finding that genocide was not proved in that case, not a declaration that the atrocities were lawful.
fact_questions.source_name: International Court of Justice — Croatia v. Serbia case overview
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Provides a concrete atrocity case in which the genocide allegation failed on its elements.

fact_questions.prompt: In the Cambodian tribunal’s 2018 judgment, why were genocide findings tied to the Vietnamese and Cham groups rather than automatically to every Khmer Rouge killing?
options: The findings required targeted destruction of protected groups; other atrocities were assessed under other crimes
The tribunal treated every political opponent as a separately protected group under the Genocide Convention
The tribunal required foreign citizenship, so no Cambodian victim could receive protection against genocide
The tribunal classified victims solely by the number killed at each site, without examining the intended target group
fact_questions.explanation: The judgment found genocide in relation to Vietnamese and Cham targeting and also addressed mass murder, extermination and political persecution as crimes against humanity. The broad historical label does not replace analysis of the group and intent in particular acts. These are trial findings; individual appeal outcomes differ.
fact_questions.source_name: Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia — Summary of Case 002/02 judgment, 2018
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Replaces a second near-duplicate Croatia outcome with a historical distinction between protected-group destruction and mass killing for other purposes.

fact_questions.prompt: In its 2007 Bosnia judgment, how did the ICJ distinguish Srebrenica from atrocities elsewhere in the Bosnian war?
options: Genocide was proved throughout the country because atrocities formed a widespread pattern, with Srebrenica treated only as evidence of the overall death toll
Genocide was proved at Srebrenica; the necessary intent was not proved for the other atrocities examined
Genocide was rejected at Srebrenica because the men killed were of military age, while mass expulsions elsewhere were automatically treated as genocide
The men’s military age excluded a genocide finding at Srebrenica
fact_questions.explanation: The judgment distinguished genocide proved at Srebrenica from widespread atrocities for which the necessary intent was not established. Neither the whole war nor every atrocity received one automatic label.
fact_questions.source_name: International Court of Justice — Bosnia and Herzegovina v. Serbia and Montenegro
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Shows why classification must track particular conduct and evidence rather than a war-wide body count.

fact_questions.prompt: What purpose did the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) find behind the 1999 campaign of violence and displacement against Kosovo Albanians in the Šainović case?
options: Physically destroying all ethnic Albanians wherever they lived, including outside Kosovo
Evacuating residents temporarily through a system the tribunal found fully protective and lawful
Changing Kosovo’s ethnic balance to maintain Serbian control through forced displacement
Conducting isolated unauthorized acts without any common purpose or coordinated campaign
fact_questions.explanation: The ICTY found a common purpose to change the ethnic balance through violence and displacement and convicted senior officials of crimes against humanity and war crimes. Knowing the campaign’s object explains why brutality and expulsion need not themselves prove an intent to destroy a group physically. The judgment does not universally classify every event in Kosovo.
fact_questions.source_name: International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia — Kosovo judgment summary, 26 February 2009
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Replaces recall of offence names with evidence about a brutal campaign’s purpose, the key distinction in applying the genocide definition.

fact_questions.prompt: What institution produces the commonly quoted running death toll from Gaza during the war that began in October 2023?
options: The Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics, through a separate ongoing census
Gaza’s Government Media Office, through its own tally independent of hospital records
The UN humanitarian office, through a direct registration system run by its own staff
Gaza’s Health Ministry, operating within the Hamas-run administration
fact_questions.explanation: The ministry is part of Gaza’s Hamas-run administration and draws on medical and registration systems. Its institutional setting warrants scrutiny; calling every medical record a Hamas fabrication is a separate claim requiring evidence.
fact_questions.source_name: Associated Press — How Gaza’s Health Ministry calculates the death toll
fact_questions.importance_rationale: States the provenance and governance concern accurately.
fact_questions.gateway_rationale: States the provenance and governance concern accurately.

fact_questions.prompt: Does the Gaza Health Ministry’s headline war-death total distinguish civilian deaths from combatant deaths?
options: No; the headline total includes deaths without that status breakdown
Yes; the headline figure is the civilian-only subtotal, with fighters published separately
Yes; military-age male deaths are counted as combatants before the total is released
Yes; named casualty lists record verified armed-group membership for every deceased person
fact_questions.explanation: The ministry’s aggregate toll does not separate civilians and combatants. A total of people killed must therefore not be presented as a verified civilian-only death toll.
fact_questions.source_name: Associated Press — Analysis of Gaza Health Ministry data, June 2024
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Prevents a central and consequential misuse of casualty totals.
fact_questions.gateway_rationale: Prevents a central and consequential misuse of casualty totals.

fact_questions.prompt: Under international humanitarian law, does being an adult man establish that a person killed in Gaza was a combatant?
options: Yes; adult men are presumed fighters absent occupational records
No; sex and age alone do not determine combatant status
Yes; men who ignore evacuation warnings are combatants
No; armed-group members without uniforms remain civilians
fact_questions.explanation: Civilian protection depends on status and conduct, not a demographic shortcut. Women and children are not the entire civilian population, and a sex-and-age table is not a combatant classification.
fact_questions.source_name: International Committee of the Red Cross — Conduct of hostilities and civilian protection
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Prevents treating remaining adult male deaths as a measured combatant count.

fact_questions.prompt: What did the OHCHR’s November 2024 Gaza report mean by 8,119 verified deaths in its six-month reporting period?
options: A complete death census for the reporting period, with all additional ministry-reported deaths investigated and found unsupported by any evidence
A random sample representative of all wartime deaths
A verified subset, not a complete count or representative survey
A combatant-status audit of every man on the casualty list
fact_questions.explanation: The office reported verification of individual cases for November 2023–April 2024. It found many women and children among those cases. The verification provides evidence beyond an unexamined aggregate, but the subset is not a statistical sample of the whole toll.
fact_questions.source_name: Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights — Six-month Gaza report, November 2024
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Distinguishes independent verification from both wholesale copying and a complete census.

fact_questions.prompt: What did the 2025 Lancet capture–recapture study estimate about traumatic-injury deaths in Gaza from 7 October 2023 to 30 June 2024?
options: 64,260 deaths including indirect causes through the end of 2025
About 37,000 injury deaths with no recorded undercount
186,000 individually verified civilian deaths by June 2024
About 64,260, with uncertainty, suggesting the ministry’s recorded toll undercounted deaths in that period
fact_questions.explanation: The study estimated roughly 64,260 injury deaths, with a 95% interval of 55,298–78,525. It combined overlapping lists, including ministry data and obituaries; it was not wholly independent of ministry inputs and did not resolve combatant status.
fact_questions.source_name: Jamaluddine and colleagues — Traumatic injury mortality, The Lancet, 2025
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Provides a sourced statistical check and its dependencies rather than assuming systematic inflation.

fact_questions.prompt: What did the population-representative Gaza mortality survey published in 2026 add beyond the Health Ministry’s running records?
options: Household-survey evidence estimating about 75,200 violent deaths by early January 2025, with a confidence interval
A direct recount of the ministry’s name lists, with no new household interviews and no independent basis for estimating deaths absent from those lists
A household estimate of 75,200 civilian deaths, after individually checking every reported victim against the membership records of all armed groups
A projection of 75,200 future deaths from hunger alone, produced by applying a fixed multiplier to the ministry’s recorded violent deaths
fact_questions.explanation: The study surveyed 2,000 households and estimated 75,200 violent deaths, with a 95% interval of 63,600–86,800. Sampling, missing households and recall remain limitations. It is evidence outside the ministry tally, not a civilian-combatant audit or exact census.
fact_questions.source_name: Spagat and colleagues — Population-representative Gaza mortality survey, The Lancet Global Health, 2026
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Directly tests the claim that all casualty evidence originates in Hamas’s own aggregate reporting.
fact_questions.gateway_rationale: Directly tests the claim that all casualty evidence originates in Hamas’s own aggregate reporting.

fact_questions.prompt: What was the widely circulated figure of 186,000 Gaza deaths in a July 2024 Lancet correspondence?
options: A new household-survey estimate of violent deaths already incurred by June 2024, with a population sample and confidence interval reported in the correspondence
An illustrative estimate including possible indirect deaths, not an observed count of deaths already verified
A verified compilation of 186,000 deaths already recorded by hospitals, with each person matched to a name, identity number and independent death certificate
An official revised ministry total excluding all combatants
fact_questions.explanation: The correspondence applied an indirect-to-direct mortality assumption. It was not a new field survey or a verified count, and its discussion included indirect deaths that can occur after fighting. Such projections must be distinguished from observed or survey-estimated deaths.
fact_questions.source_name: Khatib, McKee and Yusuf — Counting the dead in Gaza, The Lancet correspondence, 2024
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Prevents a prominent high estimate from being misrepresented as a measured contemporary toll.

fact_questions.prompt: What policy did Israeli Defence Minister Yoav Gallant announce for Gaza on 9 October 2023, as recorded in the ICJ’s January 2024 order?
options: An uninterrupted opening of all civilian supply crossings
A restriction confined to weapons imports while guaranteeing normal civilian supply levels
A complete siege cutting electricity, food and fuel supplies
A continuation of prewar food, electricity and fuel arrangements
fact_questions.explanation: The Court recorded Gallant’s announcement of a complete siege and supply cut-offs. The statement and ensuing policies matter to destructive-conditions allegations; the announcement alone is not a final judicial finding of genocidal intent.
fact_questions.source_name: International Court of Justice — Order of 26 January 2024, recorded official statements
fact_questions.importance_rationale: A major announced policy directly concerns the means of civilian survival.
fact_questions.gateway_rationale: A major announced policy directly concerns the means of civilian survival.

fact_questions.prompt: What war aims did Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu publicly state on 6 January 2024?
options: Negotiations alone, with military action ruled out
Immediate unconditional withdrawal without hostage release
Permanent civilian settlement as the sole stated objective
Eliminating Hamas, returning hostages and preventing future threats from Gaza
fact_questions.explanation: Netanyahu stated those military and security objectives. Declared aims are relevant counterevidence to an allegation of group destruction, but an asserted lawful objective does not conclusively establish actual intent or the legality of every method.
fact_questions.source_name: Israeli Prime Minister’s Office — Statement of 6 January 2024
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Includes the government’s stated competing explanation without treating self-description as dispositive.
fact_questions.gateway_rationale: Includes the government’s stated competing explanation without treating self-description as dispositive.

fact_questions.prompt: What did the United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT)’s assessment based on imagery from 8 July 2025 estimate about structures in Gaza?
options: About 78% showed damage, including different degrees of destruction and damage
About 78% had been completely destroyed, with lightly damaged structures excluded
About 8% showed any damage, with most residential areas unaffected
About 78% were confirmed military facilities, based on satellite identification of their occupants
fact_questions.explanation: The imagery-based assessment estimated damage to about 78% of structures, across damage categories. This is independent physical evidence of scale; imagery alone cannot determine occupants, military necessity or genocidal intent for each strike.
fact_questions.source_name: United Nations Satellite Centre — Gaza damage assessment, 8 July 2025
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Measures destruction independently of the casualty ministry while stating what satellite evidence cannot prove.

fact_questions.prompt: What policy and infrastructure evidence underlay Human Rights Watch (HRW)’s December 2024 report on water deprivation in Gaza?
options: Changes in rainfall and drought alone, with the report excluding policies on fuel, electricity, repair access and water delivery from its analysis
Cut-offs and restrictions affecting electricity, fuel and water systems, plus destruction of water infrastructure
Only the number of reported civilian deaths, with the report making no attempt to investigate water systems or government decisions affecting them
A completed criminal trial, rather than the non-governmental organization’s investigation
fact_questions.explanation: HRW used interviews, imagery and other records to document deprivation and linked it to Israeli policies. It concluded that extermination and acts of genocide had occurred. Israel rejected genocide accusations; the NGO’s legal conclusions are not court verdicts.
fact_questions.source_name: Human Rights Watch — Extermination and Acts of Genocide, December 2024
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Examines concrete destructive living conditions rather than relying only on death totals.

fact_questions.prompt: What happened to humanitarian supplies after Israel suspended entry of goods into Gaza on 2 March 2025?
options: Only weapons imports stopped; civilian supplies continued
Only air deliveries stopped; road aid expanded
No aid processed through the UN’s Gaza mechanism was delivered during March
Only air deliveries stopped, while road deliveries expanded without interruption
fact_questions.explanation: The mechanism’s monthly report recorded no aid deliveries in March following Israel’s suspension. Israel presented the suspension as pressure over ceasefire and hostage negotiations. The record documents a policy and effect; classifying intent requires the wider evidence.
fact_questions.source_name: UN Office for Project Services — UN2720 Gaza mechanism, March 2025 overview
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Documents an extended supply restriction relevant to allegations concerning conditions of life.

fact_questions.prompt: What did the IPC conclude in August 2025 about famine in Gaza?
options: Famine confirmed in all five governorates without geographic limits
No current famine, only a conditional risk after 2026
Household hunger, but no area-level famine in Gaza Governorate
Famine was occurring in Gaza Governorate, with reasonable evidence; expansion to other governorates was projected
fact_questions.explanation: The assessment distinguished confirmed conditions in Gaza Governorate from projected expansion. Israel disputed the analysis. Food-security classification concerns hunger, malnutrition and mortality; it is not a judicial determination of genocide or its intent element.
fact_questions.source_name: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification — Gaza analysis, August 2025
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Includes a major technical finding with its geography, evidentiary qualification and disputed status.

fact_questions.prompt: How did the IPC’s December 2025 analysis describe Gaza after the October ceasefire and increased assistance?
options: Food security had improved and famine conditions were offset, although the situation remained critical
Famine conditions were unchanged everywhere because increased assistance had no effect on access to food
All food-security needs had ended, with no remaining population facing severe shortages
The earlier famine finding had been withdrawn as a confirmed fabrication rather than conditions changing
fact_questions.explanation: The analysis described improvement after the ceasefire, not full recovery or retrospective disproof of earlier conditions. The dated findings should not be presented as if all periods of the war had identical humanitarian access.
fact_questions.source_name: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification — Gaza analysis, December 2025
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Includes material improvement and aid effects that qualify a one-direction account.

fact_questions.prompt: What enabled area-specific polio vaccination campaigns in Gaza in September–November 2024?
options: A complete Gaza-wide ceasefire lasting from the beginning of September until November, during which all campaign areas remained safely accessible
Area-specific humanitarian pauses, with access limits and interruptions
Vaccination only abroad after all eligible children were evacuated
A campaign limited to southern Gaza, because no agreement was reached permitting any vaccinations in the central or northern areas of the Strip
fact_questions.explanation: The WHO documented vaccination under local pauses, with delays and inaccessible children in the north. This is evidence of humanitarian coordination, not proof that all aid was sufficient or that every other action was lawful.
fact_questions.source_name: World Health Organization — Completion of second polio vaccination round, 6 November 2024
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Includes a verified humanitarian measure relevant to assessing the overall pattern.

fact_questions.prompt: What did the Israeli military’s April 2024 investigation acknowledge about the strikes that killed seven World Central Kitchen (WCK) aid workers?
options: Deliberate targeting endorsed as lawful attacks on aid workers
The workers died in an accidental explosion of cargo inside the convoy, with the investigation finding no Israeli fire had struck their vehicles
Israeli strikes followed misidentification and serious procedural errors
Correct identification and full compliance with military procedures
fact_questions.explanation: The military acknowledged grave errors and protocol violations and disciplined officers. That admission is evidence of a particular lethal incident; its account of intent is an internal assessment, not an independent ruling on the wider campaign.
fact_questions.source_name: Israel Defense Forces — World Central Kitchen investigation, 5 April 2024
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Uses an Israeli acknowledgment of lethal misconduct while distinguishing incident-level intent from campaign-level allegations.

fact_questions.prompt: What did Human Rights Watch (HRW)’s November 2024 Gaza displacement investigation find about evacuation routes and designated safe areas?
options: Consistently safe routes and adequate shelter throughout
A finding that all temporary evacuation is legally prohibited
No link between military orders and the population’s displacement
Repeated attacks on routes and safe areas undermined the claimed protective system
fact_questions.explanation: HRW examined orders, interviews and visual evidence and found repeated attacks and inadequate conditions. Israel described evacuations as protective and militarily necessary. The report alleges forced displacement; that classification does not automatically establish genocide.
fact_questions.source_name: Human Rights Watch — Hopeless, Starving, and Besieged, November 2024
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Tests the practical safety and conditions of displacement rather than treating warnings as conclusive either way.

fact_questions.prompt: Did the ICJ’s 26 January 2024 Gaza order finally decide that Israel had committed genocide?
options: No; it ordered provisional protection of plausible rights without deciding the merits
Yes; it entered a final genocide judgment and imposed criminal sentences on Israeli officials
No; it finally dismissed the genocide case and prohibited any further examination of the allegation
Yes; it ruled that the casualty total alone conclusively established every element of genocide
fact_questions.explanation: The Court considered interim protection, plausible Convention rights and the risk of irreparable harm. It did not make a final merits finding or decide that genocide itself had been proved. Interim measures are not exoneration either.
fact_questions.source_name: International Court of Justice — Order of 26 January 2024
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Separates a major legal development from a verdict commonly attributed to it.
fact_questions.gateway_rationale: Separates a major legal development from a verdict commonly attributed to it.

fact_questions.prompt: What did ICC judges find reasonable grounds to believe about deprivation in Gaza when issuing the November 2024 Netanyahu and Gallant warrants?
options: All deprivation was an unintended consequence of combat, with no evidence linking leaders to supply decisions
The two leaders knowingly and intentionally deprived civilians of necessities including food, water and medical supplies
The allegation concerned military supplies alone, with civilian food, water and medicine explicitly excluded
A final criminal trial had proved genocidal intent beyond reasonable doubt and convicted both leaders
fact_questions.explanation: The judges found reasonable grounds concerning intentional deprivation and alleged starvation and crimes against humanity. This is substantive judicial scrutiny of policy, not a conviction or a finding of genocide. Whether group-destructive intent is established requires the separate legal test and wider evidence.
fact_questions.source_name: International Criminal Court — Reasons for warrants, 21 November 2024
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Replaces offence-category recall with what judges found about deliberate civilian deprivation and attribution to leaders.

fact_questions.prompt: In fifteen Gaza air strikes investigated for its December 2024 report, what did Amnesty International find about military objectives?
options: It verified a military objective in each strike and found no civilians among the dead
It treated every civilian building as a military target because Hamas governed Gaza
It found no evidence that those strikes were directed at military objectives
It could identify neither victims nor locations and therefore made no finding about the strikes
fact_questions.explanation: Amnesty investigated fifteen strikes between October 2023 and April 2024, reporting at least 334 civilian deaths and finding no evidence of military objectives. This is an attributed finding about selected attacks, not a representative sample of all strikes or proof of genocidal intent by itself. Israel rejected the genocide report.
fact_questions.source_name: Amnesty International — Gaza genocide investigation, December 2024
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Replaces a generic account of an NGO’s research categories with a concrete finding bearing on deliberate attacks on civilians.

fact_questions.prompt: How did the WHO describe Gaza’s hospital system when the January 2025 ceasefire began?
options: All 36 hospitals remained fully operational, with damage confined to administrative offices
Half the hospitals had closed before October 2023, while the war caused no further loss of services
Every hospital was permanently closed and no emergency treatment was being provided anywhere
Only half of the 36 hospitals remained partially operational and nearly all were damaged or partly destroyed
fact_questions.explanation: The WHO documented widespread physical damage and severe loss of functioning healthcare, alongside needs for repairs, fuel, equipment and staff. This bears on serious harm and survival conditions. It does not independently establish the cause, military justification or intent behind each facility’s damage.
fact_questions.source_name: World Health Organization — Gaza health-system assessment, 19 January 2025
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Replaces recall of B’Tselem’s conclusion with directly relevant evidence of health-system damage and civilian survival conditions.

fact_questions.prompt: What disagreement over Gaza’s population did the US State Department describe in January 2024?
options: Smotrich and Ben-Gvir advocated resettlement outside Gaza, while other Israeli officials represented that this was not government policy
Every Israeli official endorsed permanent external resettlement as a formally adopted government policy
Smotrich and Ben-Gvir opposed external resettlement while the prime minister told the US it was required
The disagreement concerned only temporary evacuation between Gaza neighbourhoods, not movement outside Gaza
fact_questions.explanation: The State Department rejected the ministers’ resettlement statements and said they contradicted the policy represented by the prime minister and others. The dispute matters to attributing intent: an official’s statement, government policy and implementation require separate evidence. Expulsion itself is also distinct from physical destruction.
fact_questions.source_name: US Department of State — Press briefing, 3 January 2024
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Replaces another institution-status question with evidence and counterevidence about population policy and the authority behind contested official statements.

fact_questions.prompt: In Israel’s January 2024 defence against the genocide allegation, how did its lawyers characterize inflammatory quotations from officials?
options: Authentic destruction orders justified as lawful retaliation
They did not establish operational policy or intent to destroy the group
They had been fabricated in their entirety, and Israel’s defence therefore did not address the speakers’ context, authority or subsequent government policy
They were irrelevant as a legal category, because Israel argued that public statements can never be used to infer intent under the Genocide Convention
fact_questions.explanation: Israel argued that selected statements were being mischaracterized and emphasized military objectives and protective measures. Whether particular speakers, context, authority and subsequent conduct support that defence requires evidence; neither quotation nor denial should be treated as self-proving.
fact_questions.source_name: Associated Press — Israel’s defence at the International Court of Justice, 12 January 2024
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Includes the substantive defence concerning attribution and intent rather than only a blanket rejection.

fact_questions.prompt: If Palestinian armed groups unlawfully use civilian areas to shield military operations, what happens to Israel’s obligations toward civilians there?
options: Civilian protection is suspended across the surrounding district
All attacks are prohibited even on definite military objectives
Civilian-protection obligations still apply to the attacking force
The attacking force must provide warnings but can then disregard proportionality whenever civilians remain near the military objective being attacked
fact_questions.explanation: Using human shields is prohibited. It does not remove the other side’s obligations to protect civilians. The same conduct can require assessing military context and protective duties; neither Hamas’s crimes nor a genocide allegation substitutes for that assessment.
fact_questions.source_name: International Committee of the Red Cross — How humanitarian law applies in Israel and the occupied territories
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Keeps relevant military context from becoming an unlimited exemption from civilian protection.

fact_questions.prompt: What did the World Food Programme (WFP) report about the additional route, Erez crossing and Ashdod port used to supply northern Gaza in April 2024?
options: The routes were never used and northern deliveries stayed suspended
The routes replaced earlier ones without increasing total aid
Normal commercial supply was restored and all emergency needs ended
The additional routes helped it double aid to the north, although humanitarian needs and access problems remained
fact_questions.explanation: The agency reported expanded aid through additional access routes. This is evidence against an account of uninterrupted total closure, but aid entry does not alone demonstrate adequacy, equitable distribution or absence of genocidal intent.
fact_questions.source_name: World Food Programme — Gaza update, 17 May 2024
fact_questions.importance_rationale: Includes a concrete humanitarian expansion with limits, avoiding absolute claims about either closure or relief.
